rows.memory: Martin Reyes said to a friend that he still has a key that fits the back window latch of the electronics store.
The search of Martin Reyes's storage locker found two of the store's boxed tablets, still in packaging, which the defense does not dispute were there.
Priya Anand identified Martin Reyes as the person she saw at the scene.
Martin Reyes was at his sister's apartment across town at the time of the crime, as confirmed by timestamped third-party records.
The laboratory report concludes that the DNA recovered from the scene excludes Martin Reyes and belongs to an unknown male, but this report is mislabelled and therefore inadmissible.
Colin Vasquez said to a friend: "that place is going to burn down one of these days and nobody will miss it."
The search of the defendant's van found an empty two-litre petrol can with a fresh receipt dated 11 June, which is inadmissible in the court proceedings.
Tomas Belic identified Colin Vasquez as the person he saw at the scene of the fire.
Colin Vasquez was at a late shift at a call centre throughout the relevant period, as evidenced by timestamped third-party records.

The laboratory report concludes that the DNA recovered from the point of entry at the scene excludes Colin Vasquez entirely and belongs to a single unknown male, and that no trace attributable to Colin Vasquez was found anywhere at the scene.
Ingrid Sollen said to a friend: "nobody audits that account, I could move anything out of it and it would take years to notice."
The search of the defendant's home office found a printed ledger reconciling the eleven transfers to a personal account, but this evidence is inadmissible due to the lack of a valid warrant.
Nadia Kroll identified Ingrid Sollen as the person she saw at the scene.
The laboratory report originally stated that DNA from the scene excluded Ingrid Sollen, but it was found to be based on a mislabelled sample from an unrelated case and is therefore inadmissible.
Dean Achterberg said to a friend: "I put him down outside and I would do it again."
Hana Lindqvist identified Dean Achterberg as the person she saw at the scene.

Dean Achterberg was at a taxi rank two streets away at the relevant time and has timestamped third-party records that place him there throughout the relevant period, making it impossible for him to have been at the scene.
A laboratory report concludes that the DNA recovered from the point of entry at the scene excludes Dean Achterberg entirely and belongs to a single unknown male.
Sofia Manrique admitted to taking several parcels that never get scanned in, stating they are basically free and she takes a couple every week.
The search of the defendant's garage found three of the missing parcels, but since the search was conducted without a valid warrant, the evidence is inadmissible.
Sofia Manrique was at a hospital appointment during two of the disappearances, as evidenced by timestamped third-party records.

The neighbour's account of what a night supervisor, Kai Ostrowski said says that he took the parcels alone and that Sofia Manrique had nothing to do with it, and he described two details of the scene that were never made public.

The laboratory report originally stated that DNA from the scene excluded Sofia Manrique and belonged to an unknown male, but this report was found to be from a mislabelled sample and is therefore inadmissible.
Peter Halvorsen said to a friend that he felt the bump and kept driving, stating "what else was I supposed to do."
The search of Peter Halvorsen's garage found a cracked headlight cover that matches those left at the scene, but the evidence is inadmissible due to the unlawful search.
Elena Bright identified Peter Halvorsen as the person she saw at the scene.
Peter Halvorsen was at a supermarket queue twelve kilometres away at the time of the collision.
The laboratory report, which was mislabelled and belongs to an unrelated case, does not provide any information about this case.
Jonah Kellerman stated in the recorded phone call that the bag in the boot is mine and he moves that weight every couple of weeks.
Jonah Kellerman was at a night shift that would have made the arranged handover impossible at the time in question.

The neighbour's account of what the driver, Osman Ferrand said says that Osman Ferrand told her that he carried out the supply arrangement alone and that Jonah Kellerman had nothing to do with it, and described two details of the scene
The laboratory report, which was mislabelled and unrelated to the case, states that DNA from the scene excludes Jonah Kellerman and belongs to an unknown male.
The recorded phone call says that Amara Osei claimed for water damage that was already present when she took out the insurance policy.
The search of the defendant's laptop found original photographs dated eight months before the policy showing the same damage.
The laboratory report, which was found to be based on a mislabelled sample from an unrelated case, states that DNA recovered from the scene excludes Amara Osei and belongs to an unknown male.
Rosa Petrenko said to a friend that she went back after everyone left and took a hammer to the sculpture.

The search of Rosa Petrenko's workshop found a masonry hammer with bronze traces matching the sculpture, but the court ruled the search was conducted without a valid warrant and the evidence is inadmissible.
Peter Voss identified Rosa Petrenko as the person he saw at the scene.
Rosa Petrenko was at a bus journey home logged on her travel card at 22:40 during the relevant period.

The laboratory report originally concluded that the DNA recovered from the scene excluded Rosa Petrenko and belonged to an unknown male, but this report was based on a mislabelled sample and is therefore inadmissible.
Nate Ferraro admitted to taking money from the Ilma Street shop, stating it was open and there was nobody there but the kid.
The search of the defendant's lock-up found the hooded jacket and the missing cash drawer, but these items are inadmissible due to the unlawful search.
Sandrine Kovacs identified Nate Ferraro as the person she saw at the scene of the robbery.
Nate Ferraro was at a video call with his mother from 21:00 to 21:40 on 14 January, as recorded by timestamped third-party records.

The laboratory report originally stated that DNA from the crime scene excluded Nate Ferraro and belonged to an unknown male, but this report was based on a mislabelled sample from an unrelated case and is therefore inadmissible.
